source_text: Tigna domorum nostrarum cedrina, laquearia nostra cypressina. Domus animae vel ecclesiae trabibus fidei et spei fulcitur; laquearia caritatis. Cedrus et cypressus imputribilia ligna sunt, quia virtutes theologicae non putrescunt. Haec ad clausulam Libri Secundi pertinent, ubi sponsa iam non solum de nigredine, sed de ornatu communis habitationis cum sponso loquitur.
pass_a_gloss: Beams of-houses our cedar, paneling our cypress. House of-soul or of-church with-beams of-faith and of-hope is-upheld; paneling of-charity...
pass_b_english: [[The beams of our houses are cedar, our paneling cypress >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:17]]. The soul’s or church’s house is upheld by beams of faith and hope; the paneling is charity. Cedar and cypress are woods that do not rot, because the theological virtues do not decay. These belong to the close of the Second Book, where the Bride speaks no longer only of blackness, but of the adornment of a shared dwelling with the Bridegroom.
